ruling.recommended_action: Refund $4.41 to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the second off-route segment; keep the metered fare otherwise unchanged.
ruling.reasoning:
SAFETY SCREEN: I read the complaint, the driver's post-trip statement [F9] and the (empty) chat record [F8]. Nothing in any of them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — F9 is a route/congestion excuse, the complaint is a billing grievance. safety_concern = none [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

EVIDENCE: the record settles everything the ruling needs — two measured off-route segments [F3][F4], the incident record with its location and report time [F12], the metered fare components [F7], and the absence of any chat [F8]. evidence_status = sufficient, no gap.

LIABILITY, SEGMENT 1 (21:42–21:49): the trace marks RD-4(a) ✓ for [F3]: the LTA Accident record [F12] is reported 21:26 (before the 21:42 segment start), sits 0 m from the optimal route on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, and is still live in the trip window — the very corridor the optimal route uses. That is a "reasonable cause" on the replaced stretch, so this segment is exempt under [RD-4] and no refund attaches to its 2.69 km. A speed band alone would not exempt it [F11][RD-4(b)], and I did not rely on that.

LIABILITY, SEGMENT 2 (22:02–22:09): the trace marks RD-4(a) ✗ for [F4] — no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch of that segment; and RD-4(b) excludes a band-only excuse. The driver's "same avoidance" argument for this later 4.57 km loop is a claim in a post-trip statement [F9], and both corridors were merely slow, not blocked, in that window (KPE band 4, PIE band 5 [F11][F10]), so a band or the driver's narrative cannot extend a single 21:26 incident into a 43-minute blanket exemption [RD-4(c)][RD-1]. Consent is absent: there is no in-app chat at all [F8], so there is no rider message sent before 22:02 consenting to anything, and the driver's statement that it was unavoidable is a claim, not consent [F9][RD-5][G11]. This segment is therefore an unexempt deviation and is refundable.

AMOUNT: this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the excess kilometres pass into the fare [F7][RD-2]. The trace gives the rate as the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km: $31.84 ÷ 22.58 km = $1.41008.../km (unrounded). Only the unexempt segment's extra_km is refunded: 3.13 km × $1.41008.../km = $4.4136 → $4.41 [F4][F7][RD-2]. The $9.45 in [F5] is the billed excess for all 6.70 km and is not the refund base; the corridor slack outside the measured segments is not refunded [RD-2].

FLAG: the trace shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F15], so RD-6's "repeated breach" condition is not met and no account flag is added; the $0.00 waiting fee [F7] and 1.0× surge [F6] leave no FARE-1 item in dispute [FARE-1].

segment_findings.reason: RD-4(a): the LTA Accident record [F12] on the Kallang Paya Lebar Expressway, 0 m from the optimal route and reported 21:26, is before the 21:42 segment start and still live in the trip window; slow band [F11] is only corroboration. The segment is the measured stretch around that replaced portion, so it is exempt [RD-4(a)] and its 2.69 extra km is not refundable.

22:02–22:09 has no qualifying incident on its replaced stretch [RD-4(a) ✗ per F12] and a speed band alone does not exempt [F10][F11][RD-4(b)]; the driver's avoidance story appears only in a post-trip statement [F9], which is a claim, not consent [RD-5][G11]; the chat record is empty [F8], so no rider message before 22:02 agreed to this route. The segment is an unexempt deviation refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: RD-1 requires each off-route segment to be reviewed individually and RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of segments no exemption covers; the +6.7 km / +42% aggregate [F1][F2] does not itself set the refund, and segment 1 is exempt [F3][F12][RD-4].
Partially rejected: one of the two segments is exempt — the 21:42–21:49 segment is covered by the RD-4(a) incident record [F3][F12].
Accepted in substance and adopted: the accident record [F12] exempts only the segment it replaced; it does not extend to 22:02–22:09 [F4].
The $9.45 in [F5] is the billed excess for all 6.70 excess km, not the refund base; RD-2 refunds only the unexempt segment's extra_km × the trip rate [F4][F7].
Not needed for the outcome: weather [F13] is neutral; the exemption for segment 1 rests on the incident record [F12], not on weather.
Rejected: [F15] shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so RD-6's repeated-breach condition is not met and no flag_account is added.
Accepted on the flag point ([F15], RD-6 not met) but not on the merits — the driver's profile cannot authorise extra metered distance [F1][F7][RD-1][RD-2].
Rejected in its conclusion: absence of an in-app objection [F8] does not convert silence into the rider consent RD-5 requires, so segment 2 still counts.

Rejected: extending the single 21:26 incident [F12] to the 22:02–22:09 segment [F4] rests only on the driver's post-trip statement [F9] plus slow bands [F10][F11], and RD-4(b) denies a band-only exemption; no incident record supports that window.
Rejected as a ground of exemption: fair weather [F13] with 0.0 mm rain removes a weather excuse and supplies none of its own [RD-4].
Accepted on method (refund = unexempt extra_km × $1.4101/km per [F7]); applying it, the amount is $4.41, not $0.
